content.text:
**What I read:** `input/disclosure.md`, `input/conversation.md`, `input/brief.md`, `input/request.md`; all ten `draft/` sections plus `numerals.md`; all four figure briefs; and all ten `prior_art/` files (every `[REF:]` key in the draft is in `prior_art/INDEX.md` and I checked each characterisation against its file).

**On the figures:** there are no `rendered-*.png` files in `figures/` and no `review/figure-audit-evidence.json` — only the four Markdown briefs. So no pixel-level verification was possible; that matches the two mechanical failures you already have, and I have not re-reported it as a finding. Within the briefs themselves the internal agreement holds: the FIG. 1 cutting-plane description (broken line, designation "2" at both ends, no leader, both arrows pointing left) matches FIG. 2's "taken on line 2-2 … viewed in the direction of the arrows"; every numeral in `numerals.md` (16 entries) appears in at least one brief; no numeral labels two different parts; nothing the drawings section or detailed description says a figure shows is missing from that figure's brief.

**Source ledger result:** numerals 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 22, 30, 32, 40 and the elements they name all trace verbatim to the disclosure's numbered paragraph; 50 (workpiece), 100 (the lifter) and 202–210 (method steps) are drafting numerals for the disclosed panel, the disclosed device, and the operation of the disclosed device. Nothing new is numbered — no passage, chamber, branch, sensing point, sign convention, modality, dimension or threshold value has been added, which is what the prior round was rejected for.

**Citations:** nine of the ten characterisations check out sentence-by-sentence against the reference files. One does not.

input.summary: The draft is largely faithful to the inventor's disclosure and adds no new numbered structure, sensing location, sign convention, threshold value, indicator modality or dimension; the reference-numeral scheme (16 numerals) is internally consistent across numerals.md, the detailed description and all four figure briefs, and terminology ("cordless handheld vacuum lifter 100", "flexible sealing lip 12", "workpiece 50") is used one-name-per-thing throughout. Nine of the ten prior-art characterisations in the Background are supported sentence-for-sentence by the corresponding prior_art/ file. Three defects: (1) critical — the Background and the detailed description both assert that a pump-restart device tells the user nothing as the grip decays, which is contradicted by US-10625955-B2 as quoted in its own prior_art file and by the draft's own earlier summary of that reference; (2) minor — the specification asserts that the warning vacuum is "fixed by reference to the release vacuum" and that the reserve exists "by construction", a threshold-derivation assertion the disclosure does not make (it states only the outcome, that the indicator warns before the load can be dropped); (3) minor — dependent claim 3's sealing relationship is supported only by candidate-written description text. Note that figures/ contains only the four Markdown briefs: there are no rendered-*.png sheets and no review/figure-audit-evidence.json, so no pixel, OCR, leader or hatch verification was possible (this matches the two mechanical failures already reported and is not repeated as a finding).

findings.title: Background and detailed description assert the restart-threshold devices warn nobody, contradicting US-10625955-B2 and the draft's own summary of it
findings.where: draft/05-background.md, final analysis paragraph (line 23); draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "This is a different design decision" (line 19)
findings.detail: The Background states that when the leak exceeds pump capacity in the known powered devices "the user is told nothing until the panel is gone", and the detailed description repeats that such a device runs "all the way past the release vacuum without ever telling the user that the grip is going". prior_art/US-10625955-B2.md contradicts this: its claim 10 recites that "when the control unit determines that the pressure of the sealed space is smaller than the low predetermined pressure based on the instant pressure information, the control unit transmits warning information to the external electronic device" - i.e. that reference does issue a pressure-triggered warning on exactly the condition described (pressure below the low predetermined pressure, which is the condition that persists when the leak beats the pump). The draft itself accurately reports this two paragraphs earlier, so the passage is both an unsupported characterisation of a cited reference and internally inconsistent with the Background's own summary of the same reference. The honest distinction the draft is entitled to - that the low predetermined pressure is a pump-restart value not related to the vacuum still needed to hold the load - is already made in the same sentence and survives the correction.
findings.evidence: Background: "If the leak is larger than the pump can make up - a torn lip, a dusty or porous panel, a cracked substrate - the pump simply runs while the grip continues to decay, and the user is told nothing until the panel is gone." Background, earlier: "A warning unit is described as being operated when the detected battery power is below a predetermined battery power, and warning information relating to pressure is described as being transmitted to an external electronic device [REF:US-10625955-B2]." Detailed description: "a device that answers its crossing by running its pump will, when the leak is larger than the pump can make up, run the pump all the way past the release vacuum without ever telling the user that the grip is going."
findings.fix: In draft/05-background.md replace "and the user is told nothing until the panel is gone" with "and any signal that is given is tied to the low predetermined pressure at which the pump is restarted, or is transmitted to an external electronic device, rather than to the vacuum still needed to hold the load". In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace "without ever telling the user that the grip is going" with "while any signal it gives remains tied to the value at which the pump is restarted rather than to the grip that remains".

findings.title: Specification asserts how the warning threshold is derived ("fixed by reference to the release vacuum", "by construction"), which the disclosure does not state
findings.detail: The disclosure states an outcome only: "The warning indicator 32 is configured to warn a user before a load can be dropped." The claims stay with that outcome, reciting a warning vacuum "reached before a release vacuum at which the suction cup ceases to retain the load", and the description expressly equates the release vacuum with "the vacuum at which the load can be dropped", so the claimed ordering is a faithful restatement. What is not traceable is the further assertion about how the warning level is arrived at - that it is "fixed by reference to" the release vacuum and that the reserve therefore "exists by construction" - which describes a threshold-setting method the inventor never disclosed. It also closely tracks the search's own words in input/request.md ("warning threshold defined relative to load-release vacuum rather than working vacuum"), which that file directs the drafter to treat "as a pointer to look in input/disclosure.md, never as text to import". I mark this minor because the assertion is arguably co-extensive with the disclosed "configured to warn ... before a load can be dropped"; the fix costs the draft nothing.
findings.evidence: Summary: "The warning vacuum is thus fixed by reference to the release vacuum, and not by reference to the vacuum at which a pump would be asked to run again." Detailed description: "Nothing in the cordless handheld vacuum lifter 100 has to intervene and nothing has to be fast, because the reserve is what buys the time, and the reserve exists by construction from where the warning vacuum has been fixed." Disclosure: "The warning indicator 32 is configured to warn a user before a load can be dropped."
findings.fix: Reword to the disclosed outcome without asserting a derivation: in the Summary, "The warning vacuum is a vacuum which the decaying vacuum reaches before the release vacuum, and not the vacuum at which a pump would be asked to run again." In the detailed description, replace "the reserve exists by construction from where the warning vacuum has been fixed" with "the reserve is the grip that remains between the warning vacuum and the release vacuum", and replace the two later occurrences of "Fixing the warning vacuum by reference to the release vacuum" with "Activating the warning indicator 32 while the suction cup 10 is still retaining the load".

findings.title: Claim 3's sealing relationship rests only on description text the candidate supplied
findings.detail: Claim 3 recites that the flexible sealing lip "closes the suction cup against a face of the workpiece". Its only antecedent is a sentence the candidate wrote in the detailed description; the disclosure says only that the suction cup carries a flexible sealing lip and that the pump draws air through a port to create a vacuum, and never states that the lip is placed against a face of the panel or that it closes the cup against that face. The function is close to definitional for a "flexible sealing lip", which is why I mark this minor rather than critical, but as drafted claim 3 adds no relationship that claim 1 does not already carry (claim 1 already recites the vacuum created "between the suction cup and a workpiece against which the flexible sealing lip is placed"), so it can be brought back to disclosed wording at no cost in scope.
findings.evidence: Claim 3: "The cordless handheld vacuum lifter of claim 1, wherein the flexible sealing lip closes the suction cup against a face of the workpiece when the flexible sealing lip is placed against that face." Disclosure: "The lifter includes a suction cup 10 that carries a flexible sealing lip 12 on a rigid body 14."
findings.fix: Recast claim 3 in the disclosure's own terms, e.g. "The cordless handheld vacuum lifter of claim 1, wherein the workpiece is a panel and the flexible sealing lip is placed against a face of the panel.", and correspondingly trim the detailed-description sentence to "The flexible sealing lip 12 is placed against the face of the workpiece 50."

structured_output.summary: The draft is largely faithful to the inventor's disclosure and adds no new numbered structure, sensing location, sign convention, threshold value, indicator modality or dimension; the reference-numeral scheme (16 numerals) is internally consistent across numerals.md, the detailed description and all four figure briefs, and terminology ("cordless handheld vacuum lifter 100", "flexible sealing lip 12", "workpiece 50") is used one-name-per-thing throughout. Nine of the ten prior-art characterisations in the Background are supported sentence-for-sentence by the corresponding prior_art/ file. Three defects: (1) critical — the Background and the detailed description both assert that a pump-restart device tells the user nothing as the grip decays, which is contradicted by US-10625955-B2 as quoted in its own prior_art file and by the draft's own earlier summary of that reference; (2) minor — the specification asserts that the warning vacuum is "fixed by reference to the release vacuum" and that the reserve exists "by construction", a threshold-derivation assertion the disclosure does not make (it states only the outcome, that the indicator warns before the load can be dropped); (3) minor — dependent claim 3's sealing relationship is supported only by candidate-written description text. Note that figures/ contains only the four Markdown briefs: there are no rendered-*.png sheets and no review/figure-audit-evidence.json, so no pixel, OCR, leader or hatch verification was possible (this matches the two mechanical failures already reported and is not repeated as a finding).

findings.title: Background and detailed description assert the restart-threshold devices warn nobody, contradicting US-10625955-B2 and the draft's own summary of it
findings.where: draft/05-background.md, final analysis paragraph (line 23); draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "This is a different design decision" (line 19)
findings.detail: The Background states that when the leak exceeds pump capacity in the known powered devices "the user is told nothing until the panel is gone", and the detailed description repeats that such a device runs "all the way past the release vacuum without ever telling the user that the grip is going". prior_art/US-10625955-B2.md contradicts this: its claim 10 recites that "when the control unit determines that the pressure of the sealed space is smaller than the low predetermined pressure based on the instant pressure information, the control unit transmits warning information to the external electronic device" - i.e. that reference does issue a pressure-triggered warning on exactly the condition described (pressure below the low predetermined pressure, which is the condition that persists when the leak beats the pump). The draft itself accurately reports this two paragraphs earlier, so the passage is both an unsupported characterisation of a cited reference and internally inconsistent with the Background's own summary of the same reference. The honest distinction the draft is entitled to - that the low predetermined pressure is a pump-restart value not related to the vacuum still needed to hold the load - is already made in the same sentence and survives the correction.
findings.evidence: Background: "If the leak is larger than the pump can make up - a torn lip, a dusty or porous panel, a cracked substrate - the pump simply runs while the grip continues to decay, and the user is told nothing until the panel is gone." Background, earlier: "A warning unit is described as being operated when the detected battery power is below a predetermined battery power, and warning information relating to pressure is described as being transmitted to an external electronic device [REF:US-10625955-B2]." Detailed description: "a device that answers its crossing by running its pump will, when the leak is larger than the pump can make up, run the pump all the way past the release vacuum without ever telling the user that the grip is going."
findings.fix: In draft/05-background.md replace "and the user is told nothing until the panel is gone" with "and any signal that is given is tied to the low predetermined pressure at which the pump is restarted, or is transmitted to an external electronic device, rather than to the vacuum still needed to hold the load". In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace "without ever telling the user that the grip is going" with "while any signal it gives remains tied to the value at which the pump is restarted rather than to the grip that remains".

findings.title: Specification asserts how the warning threshold is derived ("fixed by reference to the release vacuum", "by construction"), which the disclosure does not state
findings.detail: The disclosure states an outcome only: "The warning indicator 32 is configured to warn a user before a load can be dropped." The claims stay with that outcome, reciting a warning vacuum "reached before a release vacuum at which the suction cup ceases to retain the load", and the description expressly equates the release vacuum with "the vacuum at which the load can be dropped", so the claimed ordering is a faithful restatement. What is not traceable is the further assertion about how the warning level is arrived at - that it is "fixed by reference to" the release vacuum and that the reserve therefore "exists by construction" - which describes a threshold-setting method the inventor never disclosed. It also closely tracks the search's own words in input/request.md ("warning threshold defined relative to load-release vacuum rather than working vacuum"), which that file directs the drafter to treat "as a pointer to look in input/disclosure.md, never as text to import". I mark this minor because the assertion is arguably co-extensive with the disclosed "configured to warn ... before a load can be dropped"; the fix costs the draft nothing.
findings.evidence: Summary: "The warning vacuum is thus fixed by reference to the release vacuum, and not by reference to the vacuum at which a pump would be asked to run again." Detailed description: "Nothing in the cordless handheld vacuum lifter 100 has to intervene and nothing has to be fast, because the reserve is what buys the time, and the reserve exists by construction from where the warning vacuum has been fixed." Disclosure: "The warning indicator 32 is configured to warn a user before a load can be dropped."
findings.fix: Reword to the disclosed outcome without asserting a derivation: in the Summary, "The warning vacuum is a vacuum which the decaying vacuum reaches before the release vacuum, and not the vacuum at which a pump would be asked to run again." In the detailed description, replace "the reserve exists by construction from where the warning vacuum has been fixed" with "the reserve is the grip that remains between the warning vacuum and the release vacuum", and replace the two later occurrences of "Fixing the warning vacuum by reference to the release vacuum" with "Activating the warning indicator 32 while the suction cup 10 is still retaining the load".

findings.title: Claim 3's sealing relationship rests only on description text the candidate supplied
findings.detail: Claim 3 recites that the flexible sealing lip "closes the suction cup against a face of the workpiece". Its only antecedent is a sentence the candidate wrote in the detailed description; the disclosure says only that the suction cup carries a flexible sealing lip and that the pump draws air through a port to create a vacuum, and never states that the lip is placed against a face of the panel or that it closes the cup against that face. The function is close to definitional for a "flexible sealing lip", which is why I mark this minor rather than critical, but as drafted claim 3 adds no relationship that claim 1 does not already carry (claim 1 already recites the vacuum created "between the suction cup and a workpiece against which the flexible sealing lip is placed"), so it can be brought back to disclosed wording at no cost in scope.
findings.evidence: Claim 3: "The cordless handheld vacuum lifter of claim 1, wherein the flexible sealing lip closes the suction cup against a face of the workpiece when the flexible sealing lip is placed against that face." Disclosure: "The lifter includes a suction cup 10 that carries a flexible sealing lip 12 on a rigid body 14."
findings.fix: Recast claim 3 in the disclosure's own terms, e.g. "The cordless handheld vacuum lifter of claim 1, wherein the workpiece is a panel and the flexible sealing lip is placed against a face of the panel.", and correspondingly trim the detailed-description sentence to "The flexible sealing lip 12 is placed against the face of the workpiece 50."
